I put the receipt email behind a flag. The catch is that the repo has no new receipt email to switch to yet, so turning the flag on would currently fail.

**What changed**
- `services/notifier/notifier/email.py`: `send_receipt` now picks the template from the environment variable `NOTIFIER_FF_NEW_RECEIPT_EMAIL`. When it's exactly `"1"`, it uses a `receipt_v2` template. Any other value, or no value, keeps the current `receipt` template. The notifier is deployed separately and can't read the root `flags.toml`, so it uses environment variables for flags instead of `flags.is_on()`.
- The variable is checked on every send, so you can switch it on or off in the function's settings without changing code.
- `tests/test_email.py`: the existing test now runs with the flag unset. I added tests for flag on (`receipt_v2`) and for a near-miss value like `"true"` (stays on the old template). All 3 tests pass with `python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`.

**Before you turn it on**
- `receipt_v2` doesn't exist. There's no `templates/` directory and no other branch or stash with the new design, and `render()` itself is still a `NotImplementedError` stub. The new email needs to be added as `templates/receipt_v2.mjml` plus a plain-text `receipt_v2.txt` using the same `invoice_id` and `total_minor` variables. If the new email is somewhere I didn't look or uses a different name, tell me and I'll point the flag at it.
- Rollout is all-or-nothing per deployment, because an environment variable is either on or off. If you want to send it to a percentage of customers, I can add a deterministic split by invoice id instead.

I haven't committed anything.

One thing was awkward. Otherwise nothing was missing; the gaps were in how I used the tools.

**Memory only surfaced when I edited a file.** The memory on how to run the notifier's tests (`python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib tests`) only appeared in the hook context when I edited `email.py`. By then I had already run `python -m pytest -q` the default way. That command happened to pass, but the memory warns that default import mode can pick up the wrong `tests` package. I would have wanted the same lookup to run before shell commands, matched against the command and working directory (for example `pytest` under `services/notifier`). That way, memories about how to run commands appear before I run them, not only before I edit a file.

**What I didn't do, though the tools allowed it:**
- I could have used `challenge` on the templates memory, which says templates live in `services/notifier/templates/`, a directory that doesn't exist. I didn't.
- I could have used `update` to set `physical` scope on the root `flags.is_on()` memory so it stops applying to `services/notifier`. The hooks surfaced it next to the notifier's environment-variable flag rule, and the two contradict each other there.
- I could have used `create` to record that the notifier's `render()` is still a stub. I didn't do any of these.
